title: Applied ML: Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Onboarding & Regression Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood's applied-ML evaluation best practices for the eval-harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding, quality guardrails, quantization profiles, and regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML owners, and SREs who operate model serving and validation pipelines.

Goals
- Provide a single, repeatable onboarding path for new model variants.
- Define prompt set conventions, metric baselines, and pass/fail criteria.
- Standardize quantization profile validation and performance checks.
- Define a regression triage process to root-cause quality regressions quickly.

Scope
This doc covers production-facing evaluation workflows (not research experiments):
- Eval harness CI jobs, scorecards, and artifact storage.
- Prompt set design, naming, and versioning.
- Onboarding checklist for model variants (open and licensed).
- Automated quality guardrails and manual review escalation criteria.
- Quantization profile validation (INT8/4-bit) and performance measurement.
- Regression triage runbook for model and infra-induced regressions.

1) Eval Harness: CI / Pipeline Standards
- Triggering: Every model build and every model config change must run the eval-harness pipeline. Triggers: commit to model repo, PR to inference-config, scheduled nightly smoke.
- Artifacts: Each job must upload: prompt-set results (CSV/JSON), scorecard (JSON), logs, model diff summary, and failure annotations to the eval artifacts bucket. Artifact naming: model-name/version/env/YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.
- Baseline and Canary: Define a baseline model per workload (baseline_model_id). Canary runs compare new candidate -> baseline and produce delta metrics and a statistical significance test (bootstrap or paired t-test as appropriate).

Required CI checks (fail the pipeline if not passing):
1. Safety checks: toxicity / PII detectors — fail if > threshold (toxicity_rate > 0.01 for general chat).
2. Latency regression: median p95 token latency increase > 15% against baseline.
3. Quality regressions: primary metric degradation > 2% absolute or significant by statistical test.
4. Embedding drift: cosine similarity to baseline embedding centroid < 0.85 for >= 20% of test set.

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks
- Naming and Versioning:
  - Format: <domain>-<workload>-v<semver> (e.g., support-rerank-v1).
  - Each prompt set must include metadata: domain, intent tags, expected output type (text/structured/embedding), author, created_at, and review history.
- Structure: Each prompt entry MUST include: id, prompt_template, ground_truth (if available), input_metadata, difficulty_label (easy/medium/hard), and categories (safety,/privacy/edge-case).
- Coverage checklist for a production prompt-set:
  - Positive examples (n>=50)
  - Negative/adversarial examples (n>=25)
  - Edge cases and long-context cases (n>=10)
  - Localized samples for supported locales (min 10% of set)
- Metrics recommended per workload:
  - Summarization: ROUGE-L, factuality precision (automated hallucination detector), human eval pass-rate.
  - Q&A / Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): EM@k, F1, answer hallucination rate.
  - Classification / intent: accuracy, macro-F1, confusion matrix.
  - Embeddings: average intra-class cosine, retrieval MRR.
  - Code generation: exact match, compile rate, functional test pass rate.

3) Model Onboarding Checklist (step-by-step)
- Pre-onboarding (owner: model-onboarding team)
  1. Confirm license and provenance (source artifact hash, license text).
  2. Create model metadata in model-registry: name, architecture, param-count, tokenizers, supported sequence lengths, baseline_model reference.
  3. Produce small-form spec: expected latencies on target hardware, memory footprint, recommended quantization profiles.
- Validation (owner: applied-ml / inference-engineering)
  1. Run eval-harness against baseline prompt-sets for each supported workload.
  2. Generate a scorecard and guardrail checks (see CI checks).
  3. Run performance benchmark: throughput@batch sizes, p50/p95/p99 latency on representative hardware.
  4. Run memory and KV-cache stress tests (long context > 8k tokens if supported).
- Approval & Rollout (owner: product + infra)
  1. Create rollout plan: canary percentage, region targeting, fallback model mapping.
  2. Schedule manual review with evaluation owners for any metric regression > threshold.
  3. Signoff and create canary deployment. Monitor for 72 hours before wider rollout.

Model onboarding checklist table:
| Step | Owner | SLO / Threshold | Artifact |
|---|---|---:|---|
| License check | model-onboarding | pass | provenance.txt |
| Eval harness | applied-ml | pass CI checks | scorecard.json |
| Perf benchmark | infra | p95 latency <= baseline * 1.15 | perf-report.csv |
| Safety scan | security | tox_rate <= 0.01 | safety-report.json |

4) Quality Guardrails (automated + manual)
- Automated guardrails (always-on):
  - Safety classifier thresholds (block/flag/exemption flow).
  - Semantic similarity filters to detect copy/PII leakage (embedding distance thresholds).
  - Output token limits and structured-output schema validators.
- Degraded mode behavior: If an automated guardrail trips in production, follow fallback policy:
  1. If model safety gate blocks: return templated safe response + escalate to security.
  2. If latency SLO violated: route to lower-latency variant or cached response.
  3. If quality regression suspected (scorecard delta): switch to baseline model and create regression incident.

Manual review triggers (examples):
- Repeated fail of safety checks for > 0.5% of requests in 1 hour.
- Human escalations > 5/week for a specific prompt set.
- New model causes > 3% drop in user-facing metric (CTR, completion rate) sustained > 24h.

5) Quantization Profiles and Validation
- Profile naming: <model>-<quant>-<hw>-v<semver> (e.g., llama2-7b-int8-a100-v1).
- Profiles must include: quantization method (PTQ/QAT), per-tensor/per-channel, symmetric/asymmetric, calibration dataset used (path/id), and expected degradation budget (e.g., <= 1.5% devset quality drop).
- Validation steps:
  1. Apply quantization profile to model artifact.
  2. Run eval-harness on full prompt-sets and compare to float baseline. Record metric deltas and latency/throughput improvements.
  3. Run hardware-specific perf test (p95 latency, throughput, GPU memory).
  4. Run targeted adversarial prompts to surface precision-sensitive failures.
- Quantization pass criteria:
  - Primary metric delta within degradation budget.
  - No new safety categories introduced by quantization (false positive toxicity delta < 0.005).
  - Latency or cost improvement >= 10% vs float baseline for the target hardware.

6) Regression Triage Playbook (fast path)
- Detection signals (automated): CI eval-harness failures, production scorecard drift, A/B experiment metric delta, user escalation volume spike.
- Initial triage (within 2 hours):
  1. Create a regression incident in the incidents board, tag owners (applied-ml, infra, sres).
  2. Gather artifacts: latest scorecards (candidate and baseline), perf logs, serving config, quantization profile in use, and recent deploy changelog.
  3. Reproduce: run eval-harness locally against the failing prompt-set and compare.
- Root cause checklist:
  - Model change: new weights, tokenizer change, different preprocessing?
  - Config change: temperature, max_new_tokens, sampling seeds, context-truncation.
  - Quantization/compilation: new quant profile or kernel selection.
  - Serving infra: GPU/kernel updates, batching changes, mixed-precision flags.
  - Data/regression in prompt sets: drift in ground-truth expectations.
- Remediation steps (example order):
  1. Rollback to baseline model or serving config if impact is user-visible and severe.
  2. If quantization is the suspect, re-run evaluation with float model and previous quant profile.
  3. If config drift: revert config and re-run controlled test.
  4. Open follow-up work: fix tokenizer/processing or update prompt set / metric mapping.

Postmortem requirements for significant regressions (severity P1/P2):
- Postmortem published within 7 days, include timeline, root cause, mitigation, and permanent fixes assigned.
- Add regression test cases to the canonical prompt-set and add CI guard where applicable.

Appendix: Example eval-harness CI YAML snippet
```yaml
jobs:
  eval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - checkout
      - setup-python
      - pip install -r requirements.txt
      - run: pytest tests/eval_harness --junitxml=reports/junit.xml
      - run: python tools/upload_scorecard.py --input reports/scorecard.json --dest s3://eval-artifacts/${{ matrix.model }}/
```

Appendix: Example minimal prompt JSON entry
{
  "id": "support-0001",
  "prompt_template": "Customer: {{issue}}\\nAgent:",
  "ground_truth": "We apologize for the inconvenience...",
  "difficulty": "medium",
  "categories": ["support","privacy"]
}

Maintenance and ownership
- Owner: applied-ml-and-evals team.
- Quarterly review: update baseline prompt-sets and quantization recommendations every quarter or when major model families are introduced.
- Escalation: For safety incidents, tag security-and-compliance and notify the incident response channel.
